narrative:
The model determined that you have a 27% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability exceeded the bank's acceptance threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were the loan amount you requested, your length of employment, and your installment rate as a percentage of income. Surprisingly, two of these actually worked in your favor. The amount you asked for (3,001 DM) is almost exactly average for applicants who are approved, which helped your case. Your 4–7 years of steady employment is also viewed positively compared with many approved applicants. These two elements pushed the model toward seeing you as lower risk.

However, your installment rate of 2% of disposable income was the decisive negative factor. While this rate is actually lower than the average among approved loans, the model interpreted it, in combination with your other details, as indicating higher overall risk. This single element outweighed the positive contributions from the loan size and your employment history, tipping the prediction into the denial range.

You should focus on strengthening your financial profile before reapplying. Consider requesting a smaller loan amount, building additional savings beyond your current level under 100 DM, or waiting until you have a longer employment record. These steps would likely improve your chances with future applications. (218 words)
